_readme: LISTING STATUS OVERRIDES  ·  built from a Bright MLS agent one-line export
Generated 2026-07-28 from Agent_One-Line.csv.
4596 residential listings across six South Jersey counties.
KEY FORMAT:  "NORMALIZED ADDRESS|COUNTY"
The MLS writes '11 Dalton Pl'. The state assessor writes '11 DALTON PLACE'.
Neither matches the other as raw text, so both sides get normalized to the
same canonical form before comparing: uppercase, punctuation stripped, unit
numbers removed, and street suffixes and directionals collapsed to standard
abbreviations. AVENUE and AVE both become AVE, PLACE and PL both become PL.
County is part of the key because six addresses in this export repeat across
the state. '505 N East Ave' exists in both Wenonah and Vineland.
STATUS MAPPING from the MLS export:
ACT  -> For sale
A/C  -> Under contract   (active under contract)
PND  -> Pending
Where the same address appeared more than once, the more active listing was
kept. That happened 91 times.
REFRESHING: re-export the same one-line report and regenerate. Listing status
goes stale fast, so a weekly refresh is about the minimum to stay honest.
Anything not in this file simply shows no status tag, which is the safe
default the page already uses.
BEFORE YOU PUBLISH THIS, READ THE NOTE IN THE CHAT ABOUT MLS DISPLAY RULES.
This is an agent export, not an IDX feed. Showing other brokerages' listings
on a public website is normally governed by your MLS participation agreement
and IDX rules. Confirm with your broker first. Nothing stops you using it
internally in the meantime.
